# `densitymetrics`: returns by height layer {#sec-densitymetrics}

## What it does

`densitymetrics` counts returns in a set of height layers above ground,
in every grid cell. The share of returns in each layer describes the
vertical structure of the vegetation: a stand with a dense understory has
many returns in the low layers, while a stand with a high, closed canopy
has most returns in the top layer. These layer counts are common
predictors in models of forest structure and wildlife habitat.

It computes the same per-layer density bands as `gridmetrics` with
`/strata` and `/strataraster` (@sec-gridmetrics), as a smaller, faster
tool. It also keeps the name of legacy FUSION's DensityMetrics program.

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| (second input) | `out/ground_dem.tif` | Ground surface, given as the second positional argument. `/ground:` works too. |
| `/outdir` | `out/densitymetrics` | Folder for the outputs. |
| `/output` | `dm` | Base name of the outputs (`dm_densitymetrics.tif`). Without it, the name comes from the input file. |
| `/cellsize` | `10` | Cell size, 10 ft. |
| `/output-table` | `out/densitymetrics/dm_densitymetrics.csv` | Also write the per-cell counts as a CSV table. |

: Options used in the `densitymetrics` example. {#tbl-options-densitymetrics}

The layers come from `/strata`, which was left at its default of
`0.5,2,5,10,20`. Those five break heights give six layers: below 0.5 ft,
0.5-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-20, and above 20 ft.

## Outputs

- **`dm_densitymetrics.tif`**: one band per layer, `density_stratum_00`
  (lowest) to `density_stratum_05` (highest), each holding that layer's
  returns per square unit.
- **`dm_densitymetrics.csv`**: one row per cell with its column, row,
  center coordinates, total returns (`TotalReturns`), and the count in
  each layer (`StrataCnt_0` to `StrataCnt_5`).

## Results

@fig-densitymetrics shows the returns per layer for the whole tile (top)
and each cell's share of returns by layer (bottom). On this closed-canopy
tile, most returns fall in the top layer, above 20 ft. Cells with a lower
share there line up with the canopy gaps visible in @fig-canopymodel-maps.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/densitymetrics_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-densitymetrics confirms that each cell's layer counts add up
to its total returns, that the totals across cells add up to the tile's
point count, and that the top layer's count matches R.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/densitymetrics_checks.md >}}
